baseline:
B
A transformer block is composed of two main sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise feedforward neural network (which is a type of MLP), with residual connections and layer normalization applied to each.

B
A multilayer perceptron (MLP) is a class of feedforward neural network characterized by having at least one hidden layer of neurons, situated between the input and output layers. These hidden layers use non-linear activation functions, which enable the network to learn complex, non-linear relationships in data.

B
The MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron), also known as the position-wise feed-forward network, takes the output of the attention mechanism (which are context-aware embeddings) and applies a non-linear transformation to each one. This step allows the model to process the information gathered by the attention mechanism in a more complex way, transforming the representations for the next layer.

C
The MLP's weights are trained to map specific input patterns (keys) to corresponding outputs (values), effectively storing factual knowledge as learned associations.

C
The core "knowledge" of a neural network is encoded in its parameters. During the training process, the weights (W) and biases (b) are systematically adjusted (tuned) to minimize prediction error. These final parameter values represent the learned patterns and relationships from the data, which is how the model stores and recalls information.
